name: Hawthorne Heights
label: Victory
lede: A Dayton band named after a hotel sign made Victory Records' biggest-selling debut, hit No. 3 on the Billboard 200, then sued the label that made them, all in about two years.

eras.title: A Day in the Life, then a hotel sign
eras.text: Before Hawthorne Heights there was A Day in the Life, a Dayton, Ohio band named after the Beatles song. When everyone but singer JT Woodruff quit, the band that replaced it got its name from a roadside hotel.

years.h: JT Woodruff starts A Day in the Life in Dayton, Ohio
years.p: Woodruff, Jesse Blair, Andy Saunders, Josh Bethel and Andy Lazier name the band after the Beatles song. Their demo, Four Bullets for One Girl, sells its 500 copies in two months.

years.h: A Day in the Life's last record: Paper Chromatography
years.p: A six-song EP, Paper Chromatography: The Fade from Dark to Light, follows the album Nine Reasons to Say Goodbye on Confined Records.

years.h: Everyone quits but JT Woodruff. Matt Ridenour finds a name on a hotel
years.p: New bassist Matt Ridenour spotted a Hawthorn Inn & Suites, added an "e" and "Heights", and the band agreed on Hawthorne Heights in 2003.
years.xp:
After a little success as A Day in the Life, the whole band quit except JT Woodruff, according to Wikipedia. Ridenour joined on bass and backing vocals and came up with the new name.

The line-up that made the first record: Woodruff (vocals, rhythm guitar), Ridenour (bass), Micah Carli (lead guitar), Casey Calvert (rhythm guitar, screamed vocals) and Eron Bucciarelli (drums).

eras.title: Ohio Is for Lovers on MTV
eras.text: Victory Records put out the first Hawthorne Heights album in 2004 and it sold slowly, until MTV started playing one video. That video turned a Dayton emo band into Victory's biggest-selling debut.

years.cap: The Silence in Black and White, Victory Records, 2004
years.h: The Silence in Black and White, Victory's best-selling debut
years.p: Recorded in four weeks, it sold slowly until MTV put the Ohio Is for Lovers video in rotation. It peaked at No. 56 on the Billboard 200 and went gold, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it Victory Records' highest-selling debut album, and places Hawthorne Heights among the biggest breakouts of the 2000s emo explosion. Casey Calvert's screams against JT Woodruff's melodies became the band's sound.
play: The Silence in Black and White

years.h: Niki FM and Silver Bullet keep the first album going
years.p: Victory releases two more singles from The Silence in Black and White in 2005, a year after the album came out.

eras.title: No. 3, a lawsuit, and a death on the bus
eras.text: The second album debuted at No. 3, and a Victory Records marketing stunt in the band's name nearly buried it. Hawthorne Heights sued its label that summer. The next year ended with guitarist Casey Calvert found dead on the tour bus in Washington, D.C.

q: the No. 1 slot belongs to us
Victory Records statement, in the band's name
years.src: Wikipedia: Hawthorne Heights · Wikipedia: Victory Records
years.h: Victory tells fans to hide Ne-Yo's CDs, in the band's name
years.p: In the week If Only You Were Lonely competed with [[Ne-Yo|a4a01f5d-18e7-4571-8c3a-76ec0e24e2d7]]'s In My Own Words, Victory statements urged fans to hide Ne-Yo's CD in stores. Hawthorne Heights said it never agreed.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, the statements asked fans and street team members to conceal copies of Ne-Yo's album so Hawthorne Heights could take the top chart spot. The band later said the label made the statements without their consent, and the stunt became part of their lawsuit against Victory.

years.h: If Only You Were Lonely debuts at No. 3
years.p: Hawthorne Heights' second album debuts at No. 3 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on the Independent Albums chart. The single Saying Sorry reaches No. 7 on Modern Rock and goes gold.

years.h: A Hawthorne Heights song lands on Underworld: Evolution
years.p: The Legion of Doom remixes Where Can I Stab Myself in the Ears? for the film's soundtrack, retitled with "Do I". [[Atreyu|17e137fb-59e5-4fd7-af48-afc34995396c]] is on the same soundtrack.

years.h: Hawthorne Heights tours the Nintendo Fusion Tour and Warped
years.p: Regular MTV, VH1 and Fuse rotation, the Nintendo Fusion Tour, and the Vans Warped Tour all in the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hawthorne Heights · Wikipedia: Victory Records
years.h: Hawthorne Heights quits Victory Records and sues Tony Brummel
years.p: In a website manifesto the band announces its exit and files suit alleging fraudulent accounting, breach of contract, copyright and trademark infringement, fraud and abuse.
years.xp:
In September 2006 Victory countersued for breach of contract and libel. On October 20, 2006, a Chicago judge dismissed two of the band's three main claims, finding the trademark and copyright claims unsound.

Wikipedia's Victory Records article adds that in January 2008 the label sued Virgin/EMI for $10 million in actual damages plus $25 million punitive.

years.h: Judge rules Victory has no exclusive hold on Hawthorne Heights
years.p: A federal judge rules the label holds no exclusive rights to the band's recording services. On May 17 the judge adds a catch: the band still owes Victory two albums.

years.h: Casey Calvert found dead on the tour bus in Washington, D.C.
years.p: Calvert, 26, was found before soundcheck at the 9:30 Club, a day after the tour opened in Detroit. The D.C. medical examiner ruled it an accidental combined drug intoxication.
years.xp:
The autopsy, released in December 2007, found a fatal interaction between citalopram (an antidepressant), clonazepam and an opiate; Calvert had been prescribed Vicodin for a root canal before the tour. Eron Bucciarelli said Calvert had wrestled with depression and that his medications were properly prescribed.

The band said it would not replace him. Bucciarelli added they didn't need another screamer.

eras.title: Four become one
eras.text: The lawsuit ended with Hawthorne Heights back on Victory for one more album, made as a four-piece with Micah Carli taking Casey Calvert's screams. Then the band moved to Wind-up, and Victory collected the hits.

years.h: Fragile Future: the first album without Casey Calvert
years.p: Released on Victory after the legal settlement, produced by Jeff Schneeweis. Micah Carli handles the screamed vocals; lead single Rescue Me came out July 22.
years.xp: The band wrote Four Become One and Sugar in the Engine to honor Calvert.

years.h: Hawthorne Heights and [[Atreyu|17e137fb-59e5-4fd7-af48-afc34995396c]] share Projekt Revolution
years.p: On [[Linkin Park|f59c5520-5f46-4d2c-b2c4-822eabf53419]]'s 2008 tour, Hawthorne Heights plays the Revolution Stage alongside Atreyu, Armor for Sleep, 10 Years and Street Drum Corps.

years.h: Hawthorne Heights signs to Wind-up Records
years.p: The band posts the news on MySpace, and says the next album will have a new screamer: Micah Carli.

years.h: Skeletons, the Wind-up album
years.p: Hawthorne Heights' fourth album peaks at No. 50 on the Billboard 200. Micah Carli adds ukulele and mandolin to bonus tracks; Nervous Breakdown is the single.

years.h: Victory releases Midwesterners: The Hits
years.p: Sixteen songs from Hawthorne Heights' three Victory albums, compiled by the label the band had sued.

eras.title: Cardboard Empire
eras.text: Out of the major-label system, Hawthorne Heights started its own label and put out EPs. Two of the three men who'd been there since the first album left within a year of each other.

years.h: Hawthorne Heights leaves Wind-up and starts Cardboard Empire
years.p: The band's own label plans a trilogy of EPs. Hate comes out August 23, two days after it leaked online.

years.h: Hope EP, and the first Hawthorne Heights video on MTV in years
years.p: The single New Winter becomes the band's first MTV video in nearly five years. A European tour includes an interview in a bathtub.

years.h: Zero, a concept album, and Mark McMillon joins
years.p: Released on Red River Entertainment in place of the planned third EP. Mark McMillon of The Story Changes is announced as a member, and the band plays every date of Warped Tour.

years.h: Hawthorne Heights re-records its debut acoustic
years.p: An acoustic The Silence in Black and White on InVogue Records marks ten years, launched with a tour starting at Fibber Magees in Dublin.

years.h: Drummer Eron Bucciarelli leaves Hawthorne Heights
years.p: Bucciarelli had drummed on every album since the first.

years.h: Guitarist Micah Carli quits Hawthorne Heights
years.p: Carli, who took over Casey Calvert's screams in 2008, leaves. The trilogy closes that September with the Hurt EP.

eras.title: Pure Noise and the long haul
eras.text: Down to JT Woodruff, Matt Ridenour and Mark McMillon, Hawthorne Heights found a home on Pure Noise Records and a place on the anniversary-tour circuit its own era created.

years.h: Bad Frequencies on Pure Noise
years.p: Hawthorne Heights' sixth album, led by Pink Hearts. They tour it opening Silverstein's 15th anniversary run.

years.h: The Rain Just Follows Me, produced by Cameron Webb
years.p: Ten songs; lead single Constant Dread features Brendan Murphy of Counterparts. They tour after the pandemic with Bayside and Senses Fail.

years.h: Lost Lights EP
years.p: Five new Hawthorne Heights songs on Pure Noise.

years.h: Drummer Chris Popadak leaves without an announcement
years.p: Dango Cellan of Amber Pacific drums at Hawthorne Heights' shows since.

years.h: Hawthorne Heights backs up Chiodos' 20th anniversary tour
years.p: Direct support on All's Well That Ends Well at 20. Off the road, JT Woodruff and his wife run Greenhaus Coffee in Sidney, Ohio.
